primary_sources: market data, competitor sites and docs, existing code, user interviews
what_to_attack: Problem framing accepted without evidence. Market size asserted, not sourced. 'No one else does this' claims — find three who do. Personas invented to fit the solution. Success framed so it cannot fail.

primary_sources: vendor documentation, primary sources, changelogs, release notes
what_to_attack: Stale sources presented as current — check dates. Blog summaries cited instead of vendor docs. Cherry-picked evidence: search for the disconfirming case explicitly. Conclusions that do not follow from the cited material.

primary_sources: existing code, config, CI, running system
what_to_attack: Requirements that are not testable as written. Requirements with no owner. Contradictions between FRs, and between FRs and NFRs. Requirements already satisfied by existing code — check before they are built again. Requirements assumed absent that exist but are unwired or off by default. Counts stated rather than computed.

primary_sources: existing UI code, accessibility standards, real device/browser behaviour
what_to_attack: Flows that dead-end or have no error state. Accessibility skipped on the false premise that there is no UI — enumerate every rendered surface first. Happy-path-only journeys. Designs that contradict the PRD's own constraints.

primary_sources: code, config, chart values, CI workflows, vendor docs
what_to_attack: Technology chosen for novelty rather than fit. Failure modes undocumented — for each component ask what happens when it is unavailable, slow, or lying. Silent-failure paths: can each degraded path report that it failed? Scaling claims with no numbers behind them. Architecture that contradicts what the code already does.

primary_sources: prd.md as the thing under test, existing code
what_to_attack: Stories that cannot be completed independently. Hidden cross-story dependencies. Epics with no acceptance criteria. Requirements from the PRD that appear in NO story — map every single one and name the orphans. Stories sized by optimism. HARD DEPENDENCIES: every epic, feature and story declares `Depends on:` — find one that points FORWARD (its dependency is ordered after it), one marked soft that is really hard (the dependent cannot be built correctly without it), and one field left blank rather than written `none`. Criteria: an epic or feature whose acceptance criteria are the union of its children's rather than its own, and any criterion that cannot be verified against a running system.

primary_sources: all four artifacts cross-checked against code
what_to_attack: The 'ready' verdict itself. Disagreements between the four documents. Blocking preconditions with no owner. Anything declared ready that depends on infrastructure nobody has confirmed exists.

artifacts: story file, changed files, test output
primary_sources: the running system, the diff, CI logs
what_to_attack: 'Done' claimed from local gates alone — check committed, pushed, merged, deployed. Acceptance criteria marked met with no artifact proving it. Tests that assert a status code rather than the effect. Edits that exist only in a working tree.

primary_sources: the diff itself, the full file around each hunk
what_to_attack: What the review did NOT look at. Findings marked resolved without a corresponding change. Whole-file context missed by a hunk-scoped review. Approval of a change whose failure mode is silent.

artifacts: test files, coverage reports, CI runs
primary_sources: the tests themselves, the infrastructure they run against
what_to_attack: MOCK HUNT: every test labelled integration or E2E, inspect its setup — in-memory fakes, in-process servers with stubbed downstreams, monkeypatched clients, fake databases. A mock in an integration test is a DEFECT. FALSE GREEN: a test asserting 200/non-null/startswith without exercising the artifact — if it asserts a URL, fetch it; an upload, get the object back; a token, use it. Tests that cannot fail. Coverage percentage quoted as if it were correctness. Gates that have never failed — inject a violation and prove the gate catches it.

primary_sources: sprint artifacts, commit history, incident records
what_to_attack: Root causes that are restatements of the symptom. Action items with no owner or date. Lessons recorded locally that were never generalised into a rule — the same class will recur. Successes claimed that the artifacts do not support.

primary_sources: prd.md and epics.md as things under test, existing code
what_to_attack: Stories that cannot be completed independently. Acceptance criteria that cannot be tested as written. Criteria that restate the title. Dependencies on work not yet scheduled. Context the implementer will have to guess at.

primary_sources: the story file, existing code
what_to_attack: Task files that are not self-contained — an implementer would have to read something not referenced. Acceptance criteria with no task covering them; map every one and name the orphans. Tasks whose 'done' is unobservable.

primary_sources: sprint-status.yaml, story and task files, the diff so far
what_to_attack: Change proposed without establishing the original plan was actually wrong. Work already in flight that the proposal silently invalidates. Edits proposed without a before/after. No rollback if the correction is itself wrong.

primary_sources: the repository itself — code, config, CI, dependency manifests
what_to_attack: Rules asserted that the code does not follow. Structure described that does not match the tree. Stale commands, paths or versions — run them. Absent conventions claimed as present. This file instructs every future agent, so an error here propagates into all downstream work.

primary_sources: epics.md as a thing under test, existing story and task files, git history
what_to_attack: Statuses asserted that the files contradict — check each story's own file. Stories in the plan that exist nowhere. Stories on disk missing from the plan. Ordering that ignores a real dependency. A regenerated plan silently overwriting hand-edited status.

primary_sources: the PRD's own git diff, existing code, epics.md
what_to_attack: Requirements the edit broke that it did not touch — diff the whole file, not the edited sections. Numbering and cross-references left stale. Downstream artifacts (epics, stories, architecture) now contradicting the edited PRD. Scope added under cover of an edit.

primary_sources: existing code, config, the running system
what_to_attack: 'Ready for development' asserted without saying what done looks like. Acceptance criteria absent or untestable. Existing code that already does this — check before it is built again. Speed used as a reason to skip the question of whether it is the right thing.

primary_sources: the diff itself, the full file around each hunk, the running system
what_to_attack: Changes beyond what the spec asked for. Hunk-scoped review missing whole-file context. Silent failure paths introduced. Untested code declared done. In direct mode, no spec at all to check against — say so rather than inventing one.

primary_sources: the repository itself — code, config, CI, dependency manifests
what_to_attack: Structure documented that does not match the tree. Commands, paths and versions that no longer run — run them. Components described from their names rather than their code. Documentation generated for code that no longer exists.

artifacts: the epic rollup (one row per epic acceptance criterion), the QA run evidence, epics.md
primary_sources: the RUNNING application on real infrastructure, the epic's own acceptance criteria, the closed stories and their artifacts
what_to_attack: The rollup itself: for each epic acceptance criterion, does a story actually discharge it, and is the evidence an artifact rather than a status? ORPHANS: criteria with no story under them — map every criterion and name them. UNEVIDENCED: a criterion whose only proof is a story's status. SEAMS: the epic's stories passed one at a time; exercise what crosses them — a flow spanning stories, state one leaves that another reads, a surface that regressed while a later story was built. Criteria reworded during implementation to match what got built. An epic declared complete while its own criteria were never read.

artifacts: the expectations set, the reader's map of what exists, the diff and its dispositions
primary_sources: the source the map describes, and the owner's own stated goals
what_to_attack: The SEPARATION: did the reader see the expectations? A map that agrees with them suspiciously well was anchored, and the diff is then a formality. Expectations written AFTER the machinery, describing it rather than deriving from the goal — check the provenance marks and challenge every [DERIVED] item the owner never ratified. Gaps classified as 'not built' that are only 'not on'. Machinery no expectation calls for, left unnamed because removing it is unwelcome. A diff that finds only what the known-gaps list already named, which means the review spent its cost rediscovering.
